title: In Vitro 3D Follicle Culture with Alginate Gel
author: Zhang, Zhang, et al.
materials: The equipment and reagents needed for in vitro 3D follicle culture are as follows (all reagents are listed in the Follicle Handbook [10,11], and can be stored at 4 °C for only 2 weeks). The instruments include tissue scissors, dentate tissue forceps, 35 mm dishes, 96-well cell plates, 1 mL syringes, stereoscopes, eyepieces with scales, straight microforceps, nontoothed microforceps, Pasteur pipettes, and transfusion guns. The reagents include M2 medium, dissection medium (DM), maintenance medium (MM), growth medium (GM), CaCl2 solution, and 0.25 % alginate solution (Fig. 1A). To ensure aseptic operation during follicle culture, all instruments must be sterilized, and the reagents should be filtered in advance.Fig. 1Method details of in vitro 3D follicle culture. (A) Reagent preparation for in vitro follicle culture. (B) Collect ovaries and place them in the DM dish. (C) Use 1 mL syringes or insulin injection needles to separate follicles. (D) Select early secondary follicles with the appropriate diameter and place them in a new DM dish. (E) Successively transfer follicles into an alginate washing dish and an alginate gel dish. (F) Place a small amount of 0.25 % alginate solution into a 1.5 mL eppendorf tube, and aspirate 5 µL liquid. (G) Aspirate follicles into the pipette tip. (H) Submerge the pipette tip into CaCl2 solution and quickly eject the liquid with the follicle. (I) A light milky gel will form in the CaCl2 solution. (J) Transfer alginate gel from the CaCl2 dish to the MM dish by using nontoothed microforceps. (K) Transfer follicles into a 96-well plate with toothed tissue forceps. (L) Place one mass of gel in one well and mark with culture information on the 96-well plate.Fig. 1

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Sterilize all instruments, filter all reagents, and store them at 4 °C for no more than 2 weeks. Prepare M2 medium, dissection medium (DM), maintenance medium (MM), growth medium (GM), CaCl₂ solution (room temperature, mixed by inversion), and 0.25 % (w/v) alginate solution (balanced at room temperature). Ensure a 35 mm dish, 96‑well plate, 1 mL syringes, stereoscopes, eyepieces with scales, straight and nontoothed microforceps, Pasteur pipettes, and transfusion guns are available.

substeps.instruction: Sterilize instruments (tissue scissors, forceps, etc.).
Filter all liquid reagents.
Store reagents at 4 °C, use within 2 weeks.
Make 0.25 % alginate solution, keep at room temperature.
Prepare CaCl₂ solution, keep at room temperature and invert to mix before use.

steps.title: Collect ovaries and preheat DM
steps.instruction: Preheat DM dishes on a 37 °C hot stage. Harvest ovaries from 13–15‑day‑old mice (healthy hair, normal weight) and immediately place them in the DM liquid; avoid prolonged immersion to prevent increased viscosity.

substeps.instruction: Set DM dishes to 37 °C.
Collect ovaries from the specified age mice.
Transfer ovaries to DM dish promptly.

steps.title: Mechanically isolate early secondary follicles
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL syringe or insulin injection needle, flip each ovary from the medulla side to the cortical side, cut the tissue into small blocks, and gently separate intact early secondary follicles (target diameter 110–130 µm) while preserving one circle of theca cells and any attached stromal components.

substeps.instruction: Flip ovary medulla→cortex with the needle.
Divide ovarian tissue into small blocks.
Fix a block with one needle; use the other needle to prod surrounding stroma and release the follicle.
Keep the needle bevel perpendicular to the dish bottom to avoid plastic filament adhesion.
Pre‑wet a Pasteur pipette with DM liquid before transferring follicles.

steps.title: Select follicles of target diameter
steps.instruction: Transfer isolated follicles to a new DM dish, measure their diameters with RI software and then with the eyepiece scale, and retain only early secondary follicles of approximately 110–130 µm (≈8–9 scale marks, corresponding to 130–150 µm in practice).

substeps.instruction: Place follicles in a fresh DM dish.
Measure diameter first with RI software, then confirm with eyepiece scale.
Select follicles within the desired size range.

steps.title: Prepare alginate washing and gel dishes
steps.instruction: Make two dishes: an alginate washing dish and an alginate gel dish. In each, place several 0.25 % alginate droplets at the bottom (room temperature). Optionally keep the dishes on a hot plate. Pre‑wet the Pasteur pipette with 0.25 % alginate solution before use.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.25 % alginate droplets to the washing dish.
Add 0.25 % alginate droplets to the gel dish.
Pre‑wet the pipette with alginate solution.

steps.title: Encapsulate follicles in alginate gel
steps.instruction: Place a small amount of 0.25 % alginate solution into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and aspirate exactly 5 µL. Bring the pipette tip close to a selected follicle, eject a tiny alginate volume into the droplet, then aspirate the follicle into the tip. Submerge the tip vertically in the CaCl₂ solution (room temperature, not on a hot plate) and quickly eject the follicle‑alginate mixture. Allow 2–3 min for a light milky gel to form. Use a fresh pipette tip for each follicle.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 5 µL of 0.25 % alginate into a pipette tip.
Eject a small alginate drop onto the follicle droplet.
Aspirate the follicle into the tip.
Vertically submerge tip in CaCl₂ solution; eject mixture.
Wait 2–3 min for gel formation.
Replace tip before processing the next follicle.

steps.title: Transfer alginate gels to maintenance medium
steps.instruction: Preheat a MM dish to 37 °C and add enough MM to fully submerge the gels. Using nontoothed micro‑forceps, move each alginate gel from the CaCl₂ dish into the MM dish and keep the gels temporarily in a 37 °C incubator.

substeps.instruction: Preheat MM dish to 37 °C.
Add sufficient MM liquid to cover gels.
Transfer gels with nontoothed micro‑forceps.
Incubate briefly at 37 °C.

steps.title: Set up 96‑well culture plate
steps.instruction: Preheat GM to 37 °C. Add 100 µL GM to each well of a 96‑well plate. Using dentate tissue forceps, place one alginate gel (containing a single follicle) into each well, and label the wells with culture information.

substeps.instruction: Preheat GM to 37 °C.
Dispense 100 µL GM into each well.
Transfer one gel per well with dentate tissue forceps.
Mark each well with the corresponding follicle ID.

steps.title: Culture and monitor follicle growth
steps.instruction: Place the 96‑well plate on a microscope equipped with a heated stage. On Day 0, record the longest follicle diameter. Every other day replace 50 µL of GM in each well and measure diameters on Days 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. Expect follicular cavity formation around Day 6 and diameters reaching ~400 µm by Day 10, entering a plateau stage.

substeps.instruction: Day 0: measure and record initial diameter.
Every other day: remove 50 µL GM and add fresh GM.
Measure diameters on Days 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.
Note cavity formation around Day 6.

steps.title: Perform in vitro maturation and fertilization
steps.instruction: Obtain GV‑stage oocytes from mature preovulatory follicles by acupuncture or incision, mature them in vitro according to the IVM conditions in the Follicle Handbook, then carry out IVF. Anticipate ~53 % two‑cell embryos and up to 22 % blastocysts under optimized conditions.

substeps.instruction: Collect GV‑stage oocytes.
Mature oocytes in vitro per handbook protocol.
Conduct IVF using standard procedures.

steps.title: Process follicles for molecular analyses
steps.instruction: For RT‑qPCR, immunohistochemistry, or immunofluorescence, fix follicles using manual gradient dehydration: 70 % EtOH → 80 % EtOH → 90 % EtOH → 100 % EtOH (three changes) → xylene (1:1) → xylene → xylene, keeping follicles in each solution for 2 min. Then dip in paraffin for 30 min, embed in paraffin, and slice. Be aware that preserving complete follicular structure is challenging.

substeps.instruction: Dehydrate through ethanol series (70 % → 80 % → 90 % → 100 % three times), 2 min each.
Transfer to xylene (1:1 with 100 % EtOH), then pure xylene twice, 2 min each.
Dip in paraffin for 30 min.
Embed in paraffin and section.
